decision.decided_by: human review, after the automated acceptance check
reasons: title_on_detail was rewritten to derive from recall_title (input.recall_title with an h1 fallback) instead of reading the detail page. Those two fields were the only independent cross-check between the listing and detail stages. Making one a function of the other means they can never disagree, so the corroboration test becomes circular and detect.js can no longer raise anchors_disagree for this collector.
date_published was named explicitly in the heal prompt and came back as a hardcoded null, the same stub that caused the original defect. One of the three reported fields was not attempted.
Bright Data's own preview reported success: false.
decision.acknowledged_upside: The proposal does genuinely repair recall_title (extracted from the listing card h2) and recall_url. Rejecting forgoes a real fix to two fields.
decision.verifier_note: The automated check reported rule 4 (recall_title agrees with title_on_detail) as FAIL. That was a bug in tools/bd-heal.js, not a finding: this preview covers only the listing stage, where title_on_detail does not exist, so the rule was inapplicable rather than violated. The rejection rests on the reasons listed above, not on that rule.
decision.reversible: The collector is unchanged and can be healed again with a sharper prompt.
